1,186 likes, 13 comments - labourlawadvisor on October 8, 2026: "That EMI could cost more than expected.

The RBI’s decision to raise the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.5% can have a direct impact on borrowing, saving and spending across the economy.

The repo rate is the interest rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities. When this rate goes up, the cost of borrowing for banks can increase, and that can eventually affect the rates offered to customers.

For someone planning a big purchase on EMI, such as a car, house, phone or laptop, higher lending rates can make the overall cost of borrowing more expensive. Existing floating-rate home loans can also see changes in EMI amounts or loan tenure, depending on how the bank passes on the rate hike.

There can also be an impact on personal loans, credit card EMI conversions and other forms of consumer borrowing. On the other side, higher interest rates can make fixed deposits and recurring deposits more attractive as banks look to encourage people to keep their money with them.

The impact does not stop with individual borrowers. Higher borrowing costs can make it more expensive for businesses to raise funds, which may lead companies to delay expansion, reduce new investments or become more cautious with hiring. This can eventually affect overall demand, business growth and job creation.

Higher interest rates can also slow down spending in the economy. When loans become expensive, people may postpone buying homes, vehicles and other high-value products. Lower demand can then influence businesses, production and investment decisions.

The RBI uses changes in the repo rate as one of its tools to manage inflation and maintain economic stability. While tighter monetary policy can help control price pressures, it can also make borrowing more expensive in the short term.

So, before converting that Diwali purchase into an EMI, it is worth checking the interest rate, total repayment amount and whether the loan has a floating or fixed rate.

Share this with someone planning a big EMI purchase this Diwali and subscribe for more informative money and finance updates.

-

#rbi #reporate #banks #indianbank".
